records.title: Fixed-generator positive factorizations in Wajnryb's Artin A5 quotient
records.description: We classify positive words in the five fixed standard generators of B6 modulo c=h representing c^2. The possible lengths are 20, 30 and 40, with respectively one, one and two strict Hurwitz classes. Simultaneous conjugation identifies the two length-40 classes, giving the three proposed representatives of Wajnryb's quotient question. A pure-braid linking reduction and an exhaustive exact 810-word certificate settle length 20. The classical group presentation, previously known length spectrum and Casson's twice-per-pair crossing assertion reported by Elrifai-Morton are explicitly credited. A full reproducible six-strand crossing certificate and independent controls accompany the note. Novelty of the exact complete classification is not certified by a negative literature search. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received external human peer review. The statement is restricted to fixed-generator input words, not arbitrary conjugate-factor or geometric factorizations.

records.title: Unbounded Multiplicity in the Dilatation Spectrum of Every Term of the Johnson Filtration: An Observation on a Question of Farb
records.description:
Farb asked (Question 7.6 of "Some problems on mapping class groups and moduli space") whether spec(I_g(k)), the set of the logarithms of the dilatations of the pseudo-Anosov elements of the k-th term of the Johnson filtration of the mapping class group Mod_g, has bounded multiplicity for k ≥ 3; the multiplicity of a value is the number of conjugacy classes of Mod_g which realise it. We observe that the question is answered in the negative: for every g ≥ 2, k ≥ 1 and N there are N pseudo-Anosov classes in I_g(k) with one dilatation which are pairwise non-conjugate in Mod_g, also up to inversion and in the extended mapping class group. This is an observation: the negative answer follows from the mechanism which the source itself gives for the Torelli group and the Johnson kernel (Thurston's representation of the group generated by the twists about two filling curves, equal traces of non-conjugate elements, the two curves chosen separating), applied to a two-generator subgroup of a deep term of the lower central series of that group, which the source itself places in I_g(k), with a reference to Farb, Leininger and Margalit. What the note adds is the comparison of conjugacy in the Fuchsian subgroup with conjugacy in the mapping class group, which the source leaves implicit also for k ≤ 2, written out with proofs, and explicit instances, which are computer-assisted, in exact integer arithmetic: for example, 64 classes in I_2(4) have one dilatation λ, where λ + 1/λ is an integer with 5116 digits. The answer is apparently not recorded in the literature accessible to us, and it may well be known to specialists. Question 7.7 of the source, on the simple length spectrum, is not answered. This is an unrefereed note.

Unrefereed preprint released for independent mathematical scrutiny. Publication on Zenodo does not constitute peer review. AI-assisted tools supported research, computation, proof development, and manuscript preparation. The author remains responsible for all claims and the final text.

records.title: Equal dilatations deep in the Johnson filtration: a convex-core proof
records.description:
For every fixed closed oriented surface of genus g at least 2 and every fixed finite Johnson depth k at least 3, we prove that pseudo-Anosov log-dilatation multiplicities in I_g(k), counted up to conjugacy in the full orientation-preserving mapping class group, are unbounded. This gives a negative answer to Farb's Question 7.6. A deep commutator with an explicit hyperbolic derivative yields a fixed Schottky subgroup. A compact convex core bounds conjugacy fusion inside any discrete Fuchsian overgroup, and Horowitz's universal equal-trace families supply arbitrarily many ambient classes at one common dilatation.

The same negative answer is recorded in Alper Ferudun's 11 October 2026 preprint, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23301731, which is explicitly credited. This note presents an alternative convex-core proof and makes no claim of firstness, a new existence theorem, a new mechanism, or current worldwide openness. Public-disclosure ordering and the relationship between the same-day candidate and that preprint remain unestablished. Powers are included; no ambient primitivity, simple-geodesic, single-value infinite-multiplicity, or intersection-of-all-depths claim is made. The deposit contains the paper and a portable TeX-source, complete written-proof, finite exact-diagnostic, independent-adversarial-review, integrity-verification and bounded-priority archive. Finite computations are consistency checks, not proof certificates for the infinite theorem. AI tools were used extensively in research, proof development, literature review, internal adversarial verification and writing. Unrefereed; no external human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification is claimed.
